solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Time for turkey, chicken and great wit!

blocks.note: Noel is Christmas, when turkey is eaten
chicken is slang for a timid person

explanation.surface: A festive table: turkey, chicken and sparkling conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma tempts you to read a menu, but the two birds each stand for a word.
explanation.definitionFit: The English playwright was famous for his epigrams and sharp repartee, a celebrated wit of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Not feeling skin of adult marsupial

indicators.note: the skin is the outside, so only the outer letters are kept

blocks.note: numb means without sensation
first and last letters of adult

explanation.surface: A grown animal whose hide has lost sensation.
explanation.definitionFit: This Australian pouched mammal, the banded anteater, eats termites and is a marsupial species.

clue.text: Old solver’s after something corny or crude

blocks.note: an ear of corn is the seed-bearing head
the archaic word for your, and the solver is you

explanation.surface: An elderly crossword solver chasing cheesy or vulgar jokes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the solver's word second in this down clue. 'Corny' suggests a stale joke; it means of corn.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthy humour is coarse and unrefined, matching crude in the sense of vulgar or bawdy.

clue.text: Made a brief visit with my boss where drinkers go

blocks.note: to call is to pay a short visit
the setter's boss is the editor, ED
drinkers head for the pub counter

explanation.surface: Nipping into the pub for a quick one with the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief visit' looks like one phrase, but a brief is British slang for a barrister, so 'Made a brief' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means formally admitted to practise as a barrister, the lawyer colloquially called a brief in Britain.

clue.text: American people’s lush hedging began decaying

indicators.note: something decaying breaks down, so the letters fall apart and reform
hedging means surrounding as a hedge does, enclosing the rest

blocks.note: a lush is a drunkard
the five letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Overgrown greenery around an American home that started to rot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lush' looks like an adjective for the hedge; it is a noun for a drinker. The 's stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ho-Chunk Native American nation of Wisconsin and Nebraska were historically known by this tribal name.

clue.text: English cricketer grabbing small bats here

indicators.note: grabbing takes hold of something, keeping it inside

blocks.note: Joe Root is an England batsman and former captain
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: An England cricketer catching small cricket bats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bats' sounds like cricket equipment beside the cricketer; it is the flying mammals.
explanation.definitionFit: A roost is a resting place where flying animals such as birds and these mammals settle.

clue.text: A lot of money in a minimum of four cups

definitions.note: plural: two of them make four cups

indicators.note: a lot of something is not all of it, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: brass is British slang for money

explanation.surface: Spending a fortune on just a few cups of coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: Each garment has two cups, so at least two of them are needed for four cups.
explanation.definitionFit: Each brassiere has a pair of cups, so the plural garments supply four or more.

clue.text: Cheap red clothing again put on husband

indicators.note: clothing dresses something, so it goes around it

blocks.note: ruby is a deep red colour
bis is Latin for twice, called for an encore
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A shabby red outfit worn again by someone's husband.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, A put on B means A sits above B. BIS is Latin for twice, the call for an encore.
explanation.definitionFit: Something trashy or of poor quality is shoddy and low-grade, which is what cheap means here.

clue.text: Fliers fight and fight with leader of squadron

indicators.note: the leader is at the front, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: to spar is to box or argue
a row is a quarrel
first letter of squadron

explanation.surface: Air force pilots in a dogfight led by their squadron commander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fliers' and 'squadron' suggest aircraft; the definition means small birds.
explanation.definitionFit: These small brown songbirds are birds, and birds are things that fly.

clue.text: Making use of remote sea, doing sport there

blocks.note: a channel is a stretch of sea, such as the English Channel
surfing is the sport practised on sea waves

explanation.surface: Riding waves in a far-off ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remote' looks like an adjective for the sea; it is the television remote control.
explanation.definitionFit: Flicking rapidly between television stations with the handheld controller is what this activity describes.

clue.text: Start off maths exam in lesson

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, which alone is kept

blocks.note: first letter of maths
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A teacher kicking off a lesson with a maths test.
explanation.definitionFit: The moral of a story is the lesson it teaches, a near synonym.

clue.text: Dislike of the new mobile phone Tobias uncased

indicators.note: removing a case strips the outside, leaving only the inner letters
mobile means able to move about, so these letters move into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the name without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Tobias distrusts the latest smartphone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mobile phone' reads as one thing, but mobile is the shuffle signal acting on phone.
explanation.definitionFit: From Greek roots neo (new) and phobia (fear), it names an aversion to unfamiliar things.

clue.text: Articles covering rent in jumper, say

indicators.note: one thing covering another wraps around it on both sides

blocks.note: the indefinite article A and the definite article THE
to let is to rent out

explanation.surface: Someone paying rent while wearing a sweater, or in a sweater-themed article.
explanation.walkthrough: A and THE wrap around LET. 'Jumper' suggests a sweater in British English; here it is a high jumper or long jumper.
explanation.definitionFit: A high jumper or long jumper is one example of a sports competitor, hence 'say'.

clue.text: Port with stronger flavour

blocks.note: first meaning: a Moroccan harbour city on the Strait of Gibraltar
second meaning: comparative of a word for sharp-tasting

explanation.surface: A port wine with a richer taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' suggests the fortified wine; it is a harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is a Moroccan seaport, and the comparative adjective describes something with a sharper, zestier taste.

clue.text: Whose works on slyness outperform others?

indicators.note: the word works as a verb means operates on, reworking these letters

blocks.note: stealth is sly, secret action
the five letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about which artist's paintings focus on cunning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Works' looks like a noun for artworks; it is a verb acting on whose, placed after stealth.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to attract the most attention and praise, eclipsing fellow performers.

clue.text: Insular people painter’s capturing I see

indicators.note: capturing something takes it in, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: Titian was a Venetian Renaissance painter, plus 's
ah is said on understanding something

explanation.surface: An artist's work depicting a self-centred people, glimpsed by the viewer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Insular' suggests narrow-minded; here it means living on an island. Gauguin painted them, which adds to the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Inhabitants of a Polynesian island in French Polynesia are literally island-dwellers, which is what insular means.

clue.text: Roll up large white covers, which can be felt

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the letters are read from bottom to top
something that covers goes over and around what lies beneath

blocks.note: a bap is a soft bread roll in Britain
L is the abbreviation for large
pale means whitish

explanation.surface: Rolling up big white bedcovers, which you can touch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roll up' looks like a phrasal verb, but roll is the bread and up turns it over in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tangible, able to be touched or perceived, is evident to the senses.

clue.text: Visitors of university teacher turned up in shorts

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means read from the bottom upwards
in places this part inside the next

blocks.note: U is the abbreviation for university
pupils in Britain address a male teacher as sir
tots are small measures of spirits, short drinks

explanation.surface: A university lecturer arriving in shorts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shorts' suggests trousers; it means small drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Holidaymakers travelling for pleasure are people who come to see a place, hence sightseers or guests.

clue.text: Sign letters have been lost around one’s address

indicators.note: around places the first part on both sides of the next

blocks.note: the punctuation mark showing omitted letters, as in don't
one is I, and 's is added

explanation.surface: Letters went missing somewhere around someone's home address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Address' suggests a postal address; here it is the verb, to speak to.
explanation.definitionFit: In rhetoric, the verb means to turn and speak directly to an absent person or thing, addressing them.

clue.text: It could be fairest to exclude Republican Party

indicators.note: excluding something leaves it out, so a letter is removed
it could be signals that the letters might be arranged as something else

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A political remark that it would be fairest to bar the Republicans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Republican Party' looks like one name, but Party is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish word for a festival or celebration, it now means any lively party.

clue.text: How a work of art may be set up

definitions.text: How a work of art may be
definitions.note: adjective phrase, as in a picture may be framed

blocks.clueFragment: How a work of art may be
blocks.note: first meaning: mounted behind glass in a border
second meaning: falsely incriminated

explanation.walkthrough: 'Set up' reads as hanging a picture in a gallery, but it also means stitched up for a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting is displayed in a decorative border, and an innocent person is falsely incriminated by planted evidence.

clue.text: Essentially American hero

blocks.note: per se is Latin for in itself, essentially
US is short for American

explanation.surface: Something quintessentially American: the hero.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth he slew the Gorgon Medusa and rescued Andromeda, a legendary champion.

clue.text: Endless labour by doctor with visibly reduced rate

indicators.note: endless means without its end, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: a slog is hard work
MO is a medical officer

explanation.surface: A doctor working without break, slowing down noticeably.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' could suggest childbirth beside the doctor; it is hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for slow motion, the film technique shows action at a slower speed you can watch.

clue.text: Step around stray dog

indicators.note: around places the first part on both sides of the next

blocks.note: a tier is one step of a rising series
to err is to stray from what is right

explanation.surface: Walking carefully around a stray dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stray dog' reads as a phrase, but stray is a verb in the wordplay and dog alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a breed group of small, tenacious hunting canines such as the Jack Russell.

clue.text: Dance leader with a heavenly body

blocks.note: a boss is a leader
taken as written
a nova is a star that suddenly brightens

explanation.surface: A dance partner leading someone with a gorgeous figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavenly body' suggests an attractive physique; it is a star.
explanation.definitionFit: A Brazilian musical style blending samba and jazz, also danced to as a ballroom routine.

clue.text: All told Liberal goes here to make slum

definitions.text: Liberal goes here to make slum

blocks.note: first meaning: a phrase for summing up, in short

blocks.clueFragment: Liberal goes here to make slum
blocks.note: second meaning: L placed inside a word for a total spells a word for squalid housing

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician visiting a deprived area and making it worse.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the abbreviation for Liberal; putting it into SUM gives SLUM, so the answer says where it goes.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin-derived phrase means to summarise briefly, used like 'all things considered'.

clue.text: One needs a hand at the table, wanting starter for meal

definitions.text: One needs a hand at the table

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the word loses its opening letter

blocks.note: a feast is a big meal

explanation.surface: A diner asking for help at dinner while skipping the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four players at the table are named by compass points, and each is dealt a hand.
explanation.definitionFit: In contract bridge, one of the four seated players is called by this compass direction and holds dealt cards.

clue.text: Main defenders make little effort and go slowly, holding United back

indicators.note: holding something means having it inside, so one piece sits within another
back means going the opposite way, so the combined letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: to coast is to proceed with minimal effort
to drag is to move slowly
U is the abbreviation for United, as in football club names

explanation.surface: A football team's defence slacking off while Manchester United hold out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' is the sea, not chief; 'defenders' suggests football.
explanation.definitionFit: The service patrolling the sea and shoreline protects shipping and rescues people, so they defend the main, meaning the ocean.
